signals.title: USD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme
signals.text: USD/SEK trades at 9.832, remaining well above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 9.596, 9.595, and 9.353. Broad strength following the Fed's 25bp rate increase to 4.00% drives the greenback higher, while SEK faces structural drag from persistent domestic economic misses (SEK ESI at -29.2). The G10 strength scorecard flags USD as the top weekly performer at +1.264% across 9 pairs, whereas SEK sits at the bottom at -1.107% across 2 pairs, creating a 2.371% bilateral spread. USD/SEK BEER fair value z-score at +2.48σ flags rich valuation, yet policy rate divergence (Fed 4.0% vs Riksbank 1.75%) sustains structural capital flows toward the dollar. Trade bias: Bullish USD/SEK, driven by CB rate divergence and G10 scorecard momentum. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Spread compresses below 0.80% or USD drops back below SMA20 at 9.596.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Fed-BoJ Carry + Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 156.08, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 157.02, 159.26, and 158.39. The 266bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.64% vs TONA 0.98%) and nominal differential (Fed 4.0% vs BoJ 1.0%) continue to support the dollar, supported by hawkish FOMC dot plots. However, 25-delta risk reversals print at -2.18, reflecting an aggressive options market skew for downside protection against BoJ policy tightening or intervention risk ahead of 160.00. JPY COT Leveraged Funds net short stands at -53,255 (pctl 30), despite a massive WoW buy-back of +58,042 contracts that signals short covering. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, supported by carry while VIX remains contained at 17.7. Catalyst: BoJ Rate Decision and Press Conference at ~02:30 UTC. Risk: BoJ surprises with a hawkish stance or rate hike, triggering disorderly carry liquidation below 155.00.

signals.title: GBP/USD — CB Yield Parity + Energy Shock Hedging
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3385, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3484 and 1.3455. The Fed's 25bp rate hike to 4.0% eliminates the Bank of England's (3.75%) policy rate premium, flipping the 1-month OIS carry differential to favor USD by +25bp. While UK headline inflation rose to 3.1% in August due to elevated energy prices, UK 10Y yields at 5.30% maintain a +28bp spread over US 10Y. COT positioning shows Leveraged Funds long at net +40,361 (pctl 86, z +1.02), but a WoW reduction of -7,143 contracts indicates specs are unwinding exposure. Option markets maintain a mild put skew with 1M 25d RR at -0.35, while 1M IV at 5.1% vs HV30 at 4.0% commands a +1.1% volatility risk premium. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD, following loss of central bank rate advantage and energy-driven stagflation risk. Catalyst: BoE Rate Decision and Minutes at 11:00 UTC. Risk: BoE delivers a hawkish rate increase, pushing price back above 1.3485.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT Squeeze Setup vs Retail Sentiment Extreme
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5723, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5879, 0.5858, and 0.5856. Better-than-expected Q2 GDP at +2.6% y/y provides fundamental backing for the RBNZ's hawkish stance (rate at 2.75%). COT Leveraged Funds hold a net short of -18,092 contracts at a 52-week percentile of 8 (z -1.40), indicating an extreme institutional short position that is vulnerable to a squeeze. Conversely, retail sentiment sits at an extreme 89% long, creating a sharp institutional-versus-retail divergence. Options BEER model flags NZD/USD as cheap at z=-1.80σ against fair value of 0.5854. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD, targeting a short-squeeze recovery toward moving average resistance. Catalyst: New Zealand Trade Balance release at 22:45 UTC. Risk: Broader USD strength accelerates, pushing spot below technical support at 0.5700.
